comment: Describes every setting so the GUI can render controls for it, and so docs/config.md can be generated from it. A section carrying both `page` and `keys` renders as the page -- that wins -- while the keys still reach the generated reference, which is how a setting that needs more than a control in the window is still documented as the config key it is. Deliberately the same shape as the `config` block in a widget.json, so one renderer handles built-in settings and third-party widgets alike.

sections.label: Appearance
sections.description: How the shell itself looks -- light or dark, its accent, its corners -- and the style every Qt application is drawn in. The shell's own colours change nothing outside it.

theme.mode.label: Colour scheme
theme.mode.description: auto turns the shell dark whenever the Plasma colour scheme is dark: chosen in System Settings, or switched at sunset when Plasma's global theme is set to change between a light and a dark one by itself. light and dark hold it there.

theme.accent.label: Accent
theme.accent.description: plasma is Plasma's own accent colour, which System Settings can also take from the wallpaper. Every other colour the shell uses is worked out from this one, in Material Design's roles. A colour written as #rrggbb is accepted too.

theme.translucent.label: Translucent surfaces
theme.translucent.description: The panel and its popouts let a little of what is behind them through. Off draws them solid.

theme.rounding.label: Corner rounding
theme.rounding.description: The radius of the largest surfaces -- the start menu, quick settings, a floating panel. Smaller things are rounded in proportion.

sections.label: Taskbar
sections.description: The panel: where it sits, how big it is, and the widgets that are parts of it -- the clock, the workspace pills and the window buttons. Every one of these is a configuration key, so a profile can set them by hand as well.

panel.position.label: Position
panel.position.description: Which edge the panel is anchored to.

panel.thickness.label: Thickness
panel.thickness.description: Height of a horizontal panel, width of a vertical one. Its buttons grow and shrink with it.

panel.style.label: Style
panel.style.description: full is a strip along the whole edge. floating is a rounded bar held clear of the edge. islands draws no bar at all: each zone -- the start button and workspaces, the windows, the tray and clock -- is a rounded island of its own.

panel.spacing.label: Spacing
panel.spacing.description: The gap between widgets, in pixels.

panel.iconSize.label: Tray icon size
panel.iconSize.description: The size of the tray's and the status icons, in pixels.

panel.revealOnHover.label: Reveal on hover
panel.revealOnHover.description: With hiding on, the panel comes back when the pointer reaches the screen edge. Off, it comes back only when something opens from it -- the launcher from a key, say.

panel.autoHide.label: Hide until pointed at
panel.autoHide.description: The panel shrinks to a sliver and comes back when the pointer reaches the screen edge. It reserves no space while hidden, so windows use the whole screen.

sections.label: Windows
sections.description: What KWin does with windows: how focus is given, when one is raised, where a new one lands, and whether a maximised window keeps its border. These are KWin's own settings, written through the ledger by `rmpr windows behaviour`, so every change can be undone. Window gaps, rounded window corners and tiling layouts are not KWin's to give, and are not offered here.

sections.label: Launcher
sections.description: What opens when you press the start button, and what opens when you search.

launcher.provider.label: Application menu
launcher.provider.description: Kickoff is Plasma's own menu, but it opens at whichever panel holds plasmashell's launcher applet rather than at this one.

launcher.layout.label: Start menu
launcher.layout.description: How the built-in launcher's start menu is laid out. twopane: categories, pinned apps and recent files, with you, what is playing and the machine beside them. grid: pinned apps and recent files. list: every application A to Z. Only when the built-in launcher is the application menu.

launcher.actionPrefix.label: Action prefix
launcher.actionPrefix.description: Typed first in the built-in search, it offers the shell's actions -- the colour scheme, the wallpaper, the session, a calculator -- instead of applications.

launcher.dense.label: Compact results
launcher.dense.description: Shorter rows in the built-in search, so more fit.

launcher.hints.label: Key hints
launcher.hints.description: The keys the built-in search answers to, under its results.

launcher.pinned.label: Pinned applications
launcher.pinned.description: Desktop entry ids at the top of the built-in start menu, in this order. Empty picks a terminal, files, a browser, an editor and so on from what is installed.

launcher.kickoffMode.label: Kickoff style
launcher.kickoffMode.description: Windowed opens Kickoff as an ordinary window; slower, and it will not close itself when it loses focus.

sections.label: Notifications
sections.description: Plasma draws every notification -- under this shell's own renderer, through the Plasma services it hosts -- unless this shell is asked to draw them itself. The history remembers what went past either way, so a notification that disappeared can be read again and, with AI assist on, asked about.

notifications.server.label: Drawn by
notifications.server.description: plasma: Plasma's own notification server, as always. shell: this shell serves them and draws its own popups beside the panel, with an Ask button on each when AI assist is on. That replaces Plasma's, so it is off unless chosen. It works only under this shell's renderer, and while another program holds the notification service -- Plasma's hosted applet, or another shell's bar -- it waits for the service to be let go of rather than taking it.

notifications.popupTimeout.label: Popups stay for (seconds)
notifications.popupTimeout.description: Unless the application asks for a time of its own. Critical ones stay until closed, and the pointer resting on a popup holds it. Only when this shell draws them.

notifications.popupPosition.label: Popups appear at
notifications.popupPosition.description: auto is the right-hand end of the panel's edge, beside the clock. The centres are the middle of the top or bottom edge. Only when this shell draws them.

notifications.centreStyle.label: Notification centre
notifications.centreStyle.description: What the bell opens. grouped: one card per application, the latest on top and the rest stacked behind it. stream: every notification in order, under today, yesterday and earlier.

notifications.history.label: Keep a history
notifications.history.description: Listens on the session bus for notifications as they are sent. Nothing is taken over and nothing is stored on disk; the history lives in memory and is gone when the shell stops. Off, the listener does not run at all.

notifications.historySize.label: Remember
notifications.historySize.description: How many recent notifications to keep.

sections.label: Lock & session
sections.description: This shell's own lock screen -- off until it has been tried -- and which screen asks before the session ends. Plasma's greeter does the locking either way.

session.prompt.label: Ending the session asks with
session.prompt.description: plasma: Plasma's own logout screen, as always. shell: the shell's -- log out, restart, hibernate where the machine can, shut down -- which ends the session through Plasma's session manager all the same, so applications are still asked to save.

sections.label: Plasma services
sections.description: Plasma's notifications, its clipboard history and its device notifier live inside Plasma's system tray, and the panel this shell draws has no Plasma tray. So under this shell's own renderer they are kept running by hosting Plasma's own applets outside any panel, each showing as one icon in the tray. Nothing is reimplemented, and nothing is hosted where a Plasma tray is there to provide them.

services.hostPlasma.label: Keep Plasma's notifications, clipboard and device notifier running
services.hostPlasma.description: Off, under the quickshell renderer nothing receives notifications at all -- they are dropped, not queued -- and the clipboard widget keeps a history of its own instead of Plasma's.

sections.label: Widgets
sections.description: What appears on the panel, and in which zone.

sections.label: Tray icons
sections.description: Which tray icons sit on the panel, which go behind the chevron, and which are left out. Drag a row from one list to another.

sections.label: Screen edges
sections.description: What happens when the pointer is pushed into a corner or an edge of the screen, and whether a window dragged there snaps. KWin does all of it; this only configures KWin, and every change can be undone.

sections.label: Switching windows
sections.description: What Alt+Tab looks like, and which program gets Alt+Tab and Meta+Tab. KWin draws the window switcher and the Overview; another shell running beside it may be holding the keys, and nothing here moves one without being asked.

sections.label: On-screen display
sections.description: The volume and brightness popup. Plasma draws it by default and works well; ours exists for the placement and animation a Plasma OSD cannot do. Turning ours on without silencing Plasma's shows both -- 'rmpr theme osd ours' silences it.

osd.enabled.label: Draw our own
osd.enabled.description: Listens to the same signals Plasma's OSD does. Nothing is taken over, and turning it off leaves Plasma exactly as it was.

sections.label: Layouts
sections.description: Shipped panel layouts. Applying one replaces your current configuration.

sections.label: Profiles
sections.description: Separate configurations you can switch between, and per-monitor overrides within each.

sections.label: Restore points
sections.description: Snapshots of your KDE configuration. Nothing here is ever deleted automatically.

sections.label: Drawn by
sections.description: What draws the panel. Only one of these can draw at a time, and switching is a real change to your desktop rather than a setting -- so it happens here, with a restore point, rather than as a value you can type.

panel.renderer.label: Drawn by
panel.renderer.description: Which of them draws the panel. Only one can, so two panels at one screen edge is not a state this can reach. Changing it by hand only tells the shell; the shell package, the applet layout and the restore point are the CLI's job -- use `rmpr renderer set`.

sections.label: AI assist
sections.description: When something breaks, hand a redacted diagnostic report to an assistant. Off by default. Nothing leaves this machine without a confirmation that shows exactly what would be sent.

ai.enabled.label: AI assist
ai.enabled.description: Turns on the 'ask' actions: in the notification history, as a global shortcut, and as `rmpr ask`. It also starts the notification listener, since a notification has to have been seen to be asked about.

ai.provider.label: Provider
ai.provider.description: `clipboard` copies the report for pasting anywhere and sends nothing. `claude-code` opens the `claude` command with the report. `ollama` asks a local model over HTTP. `custom` runs `ai.command`. Providers whose program is not installed are not offered.

ai.command.label: Custom command
ai.command.description: For the `custom` provider: a command and its arguments. `%report` is replaced with the path of the redacted bundle; without it, the bundle arrives on standard input.

ai.ollamaUrl.label: Ollama address
ai.ollamaUrl.description: Where the `ollama` provider sends its request. An address that is not this machine counts as leaving it, and is confirmed like any other.

ai.ollamaModel.label: Ollama model
ai.ollamaModel.description: Empty picks the first model Ollama lists.
